subject: ACME Bank — eval plan & recommended models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Price <samantha.price@acmebank.com>, Tom Liu <tom.liu@acmebank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: ACME Bank discovery follow-up — recommended eval plan & next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and clear priorities around accuracy on customer-facing summaries and protecting PII. Per our call, I put together a concise evaluation plan to validate model fit for the two main flows you described (agent summaries and policy-guided redaction). High-level items below, plus attached sample prompt set.

Recommended models to test:
- redwood-llama-70b (float16) — baseline for best-quality open model
- redwood-llama-70b-8bit (quantized) — cost/latency tradeoff candidate
- redwood-vicuna-13b (fp16) — faster, cheaper baseline for throughput tests
- fallback: redwood-llama-70b-seqopt for long-context cases

Suggested benchmarks & scoring:
- Primary metric: accuracy on golden summaries (ROUGE-L + human pass/fail for edge cases)
- Safety check: automated PII-detection recall/precision on redaction tasks
- Regression guardrail: threshold on mean ROUGE-L and no >5% drop vs baseline between runs

Eval setup (short):
1) You upload a CSV: columns [id, prompt, expected_response, tolerance_notes] — sample attached (acme_eval_prompt_set.csv).
2) We create an eval job in Redwood: select model variants, choose automatic scoring (ROUGE/BLEU + exact matches) and attach human-review buckets for low-confidence cases.
3) Run batch and share per-prompt breakdown + failure logs.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm you can share a 200–500 row sample in the attached CSV format (we can redact actual customer identifiers if needed).
- Confirm which SLA (latency target) you want us to prioritize for the throughput runs.
- I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Neha (solutions eng) to set up the eval environment and walk through scoring thresholds.

Attachments: acme_eval_prompt_set.csv (CSV, sample 24 rows)
Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-eval-playbooks

Thanks — I’ll pencil in a provisional kickoff for Mon, 11/23; let me know if that works.

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ACME Bank discovery follow-up — recommended eval plan & next steps

Thanks Samantha — good questions. Quick answers below and a few concrete artifacts attached.

ROUGE / scoring details:
- We run ROUGE-1/2/L using standard py-rouge defaults; we also calculate BLEU (smoothing method 1) and chrF for short responses. For summaries we prioritize ROUGE-L and human-pass rates. I attached the eval playbook with exact scoring configs.

Human review workflow:
- Redwood flags low-confidence or low-scoring prompts into a reviewer queue (CSV export). We provide a per-row tag, model score breakdown, model output, and an explanation field for reviewer notes. You can download the reviewer CSV or connect via Drive.

Regression + rollout guidance:
- Canary rollout pattern: 5% traffic on quantized variant for 48 hours with active monitoring on hallucination rate and error surface. If hallucination delta > 2% absolute vs baseline, auto-rollback.
- We recommend a secondary fallback to the full-precision model for high-risk flows (e.g., final customer-facing summaries).

Dataset format (required sample):
- CSV columns: id, prompt, expected_response, category, tolerance_notes
- id: string
- prompt: input text that replicates the downstream flow
- expected_response: canonical expected output for automated scoring
- category: flow tag (e.g., summary, redaction)
- tolerance_notes: free text that explains if partial matches are acceptable

Attached: redwood_eval_playbook.pdf (scoring configs + rollout patterns)
Attachment: acme_eval_prompt_set.csv (sample template)
Link: https://dash.redwood.ai/evals/rdw-acme-2026 — provisional eval job will appear here once we import your CSV.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 11/24 AM PT: kickoff + dataset walkthrough (Neha leads setup).
- By Thu 11/26: you share 200-row redacted sample.
- Next 5 business days: run baseline + quantized runs and share results.

If that timeline works I’ll send an invite for Tue 11/24 9:00 AM PT.

Best,
Marissa
